subject: Operational acceptance: DR sequencing and evidence needed for RFP response

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the materials submitted yesterday. As we prepare the final SOW and security appendix, our sourcing and engineering teams need more granular acceptance criteria and evidence around your multi-region failover approach. Specific items we need before Tuesday's deadline: 

- Clear RTO and RPO commitments by failure class (control plane, inference API, persisted customer artifacts).
- Detailed switchover sequence (what is automated vs manual, DNS change windows, LB drains).
- How in-flight requests and KV/prefix cache are handled — what is considered "acceptable data loss" if any.
- Artefacts: runbook excerpt showing the gating checks, a recent rehearsal log (pass/fail with timestamps), and any signed MOA/notice of acceptance from prior customers.
- Acceptance test steps you expect us to include in the SOW for sign-off (we need machine-readable test steps to include in our acceptance matrix).

Can you confirm which of the above you can provide and whether you can join a short 30-minute call Wed 05/27 to walk through the sequencing?

Best,

From: marcus_lin@redwood-inference.com
To: Paul Simmons <paul.simmons@clearwater-health.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood-inference.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-05-27T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Q: DR sequencing, acceptance criteria and evidence for multi-region failover

Paul / Jasmine — thanks. Below are our concise, concrete answers you can paste into the RFP response and SOW acceptance matrix. I also attached the rehearsal log and the signed MOA excerpt as requested.

1) Failure classes and commitments (summary):
   - Control plane outage (region-level control plane failure): RTO = 3 minutes (median), operational failover completed within 10 minutes (99th percentile) for routing to healthy control plane endpoints; RPO = near-zero for model artifacts (replicated across regions), configuration replication is synchronous across control plane cluster.
   - Inference API (serving node / worker degradation): For warm-standby pool + automated routing: RTO = median 2–5 minutes to restore full API capacity via traffic shift and autoscale; RPO = 0 for persisted request metadata; ephemeral in-flight tokenization/state is not persisted — expected acceptable loss window: up to 2 minutes of in-flight work for tail cases.
   - Persistent customer artifacts (models, customer-config, audit logs): RPO = 0 for model artifacts and configs (geo-replicated), RPO = <1 minute for audit logs (near-real-time replication), with snapshots retained per contract.

2) Switchover sequencing (high level):
   - Detection: automated anomaly detection + operator alert triggers (route to DR runbook).
   - Pre-checks: health of target region, available warm pool capacity, model variant availability, schema consistency checks, replication lag < 60s.
   - Quiesce/gating: drain new write-heavy admin tasks; perform schema lock if required for migration steps.
   - Traffic cutover: DNS-level routing via our traffic fabric with TTL tuning (we use dual-plane routing + load balancer reconfiguration). For customer critical flows we recommend a staged cutover: 5% canary -> 50% ramp -> 100% cutover with monitoring gates (latency/error thresholds).
   - Post-cutover validation: smoke tests (generation correctness, embeddings sampling), token-level throughput tests, and verification of audit-log continuity.

3) In-flight requests and cache behavior:
   - In-flight: Best-effort retries are issued by our gateway for idempotent calls. Non-idempotent operations that depend on ephemeral KV state may be lost; we classify acceptable loss as up to 2 minutes of in-flight ephemeral state for warm failovers.
   - KV/prefix cache: caches are treated as warm-standby; cache miss rates may increase briefly after failover, but consistency is preserved for persisted artifacts.

4) Acceptance tests to include in SOW (machine-readable steps):
   - Test 1 — Canary failover: Initiate a controlled failover of a single model serving shard. Pass criteria: API 95th percentile latency <= 1.2x baseline within 10 minutes; error rate <= baseline + 0.5%.
   - Test 2 — Full switchover: Execute staged cutover per runbook. Pass criteria: successful cutover to target region, no loss of persisted artifacts, audit logs contiguous (no gaps), and business-critical endpoints return expected signatures for 100 random sample requests.
   - Test 3 — Recovery validation: Bring original region back and verify bi-directional replication and consistency for models/configs; pass if validation checksums match for 99.99% of tracked objects.

5) Evidence provided (attached):
   - rehearsal-log-20260510.csv: our May dress rehearsal showing timestamps for detection->cutover->validation and post-cutover metrics.
   - signed-moa-redwood-clearwater.pdf: redacted MOA from a prior customer outlining acceptance thresholds.

Notes / caveats: we discourage expectations of zero perceived latency during DNS-level changes — for ultra-low-latency SLAs we recommend dedicated capacity with cross-region active-active configuration (available as Dedicated+ActiveActive). We can draft SOW language to map our tests to your acceptance matrix.

Attached: rehearsal-log-20260510.csv, signed-moa-redwood-clearwater.pdf

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com
To: Paul Simmons <paul.simmons@clearwater-health.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood-inference.com, marcus_lin@redwood-inference.com

Subject: Re: RFP Q: DR sequencing, acceptance criteria and evidence for multi-region failover

Paul — apologies for the slight delay; consolidating the technical checklist below so you can drop it directly into the SOW. Marcus is available for an on-demand walkthrough if you want to run the checklist during a call.

Technical checklist / machine-readable acceptance steps:
- Pre-test: Ensure test harness has API key with staging access and `test-client-id` header. Baseline measurements: capture 5-minute P95 latency and 5-minute error rate.

- Canary Failover (automation):
  1) POST /admin/v1/failover/start?shard=<shard-id>&mode=canary  
     Expected response: {"status":"initiated","shard":"<shard-id>","started_at":"<ISO>"}
  2) Verify metric exposures via Prometheus endpoint: `redwood.failover.latency_ms.p95` and `redwood.failover.error_rate`.
     Pass: `redwood.failover.latency_ms.p95` <= baseline * 1.2 within 10 minutes AND `redwood.failover.error_rate` <= baseline + 0.5%.
  3) Check audit continuity: query /audit/v1/continuity?from=<t1>&to=<t2> returns no gaps; pass if "gaps":0.

- Full Switchover (automation):
  1) POST /admin/v1/failover/start?mode=staged
     Expected response: {"status":"staged","steps": [..], "started_at":"<ISO>"}
  2) Validate staged ramp (5% -> 50% -> 100%) using `redwood.traffic.ramp_progress` metric; pass when ramp reaches 100% and `redwood.health.checks` all report OK.
  3) Validation: run 100 sample inference calls against business-critical model endpoints and assert byte-level signature match for stable prompt set.

- Recovery:
  1) POST /admin/v1/failover/rollback
     Expected response: {"status":"rollback_initiated","target":"original-region"}
  2) Verify replication checksums via /ops/v1/replication/checksums?dataset=models; pass if >= 99.99% match.

Operational/Networking notes:
- Recommended DNS TTL during cutover: 30s for staged canary; revert to 300s after validation. We use dual-plane routing and will coordinate IP announcements if required; your networking team does not need to accept new IPs for standard DNS-based cutover, but please ensure firewall rules allow outbound to `*.redwood-inference.com` IP ranges (we will provide an updated list).
- Non-idempotent example: long-running model tuning jobs that checkpoint to ephemeral storage. For these operations we recommend explicit job-ack IDs and resumable checkpoints — our API provides job checkpoint endpoints and we can include instrumented examples.

Next steps: 
- I'll upload the final machine-readable CSV for the rehearsal log and the MOA redaction to the Drive link Jasmine provided.
- We propose a witness canary on 06/12 (dry run) between 09:00–11:00 PT — if that window works we will issue the formal test plan and invite both teams.

Thanks — happy to draft SOW language if you want a first pass.

--
Laura Bennett
Customer Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com
